discovery.none: Manual selection of the exact scooter is required before any GATT write. A Ninebot Z has the same NUS trio and 5A A5/L+9 outer frame; a bare NUS fingerprint or 5A A5 header must never activate this scooter spec. After manual selection, confirm the scooter's role addresses and register reply layout before any setting write. Do not infer identity from the shared outer length/checksum framing.

identification.notes: No advertised-name matcher is established. Nordic UART is shared with the Ninebot Z EUC, InMotion V2 and unrelated peripherals, so it is a post-connect transport detail only and is deliberately not a scan axis.

device.name: Ninebot / Segway E-Scooter (BLE)
device.notes:
Ninebot / Segway ES and MAX (G30) e-scooters use the same Nordic-UART serial-over-BLE bridge as the Xiaomi M365 — see xiaomi-m365-ble.yaml for the register read/write model and the ESC/BMS register map, which are shared. Only the outer frame differs.
The Ninebot Z electric unicycle is NOT this protocol. It shares this spec's NUS trio and its 5A A5 header, clear payload length, L+9 accounting and little-endian checksum envelope. The distinction is the Z's repeating-XOR transform, role addresses and telemetry payloads versus this scooter's register layouts, not the outer length semantics. See euc-wheellog-ble.yaml (its ninebot_z frame-format block); neither NUS nor the shared outer frame may activate scooter writes.
GATT: Nordic UART service 6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e; write/RX 6e400002-...; notify/TX 6e400003-... (same as the M365).
FRAME: header 5A A5 (vs the Xiaomi 55 AA), then length, source addr, destination addr, command, argument, payload, and a 2-byte little-endian checksum. The read/write register model and the ESC-vs-battery address scheme match the Xiaomi variant.
CRYPTO: the reference library's Ninebot transport is checksum-only (no AES/CCM/nonce/ECDH). Newer G30 firmware is widely reported to add AES session encryption; that is not confirmed from a source used here and should be verified before relying on plaintext access on current units.
SAFETY: on plaintext/older units the same "commands unauthenticated over BLE" class of issue as the M365 applies (shared bus + app-only password).

openness.notes: No vendor documentation; the plaintext framing is reverse-engineered. Newer-firmware session crypto is not covered by the fetched sources.

upstream_docs.covers: The Ninebot 5A A5 framing (transport/ninebot.py) and the shared BLE link.
upstream_docs.title: Informatic/py9b

pairing.notes: Connect and write 5A A5 frames; no bond is negotiated or stored. Newer firmware adds a session-crypto handshake to the frame layer, so a client that connects successfully and then gets nothing back is looking at a firmware difference rather than a pairing failure — verify per unit.

credentials.notes: Older units gate the app only, not the bus. Newer firmware may add a session key — verify before assuming plaintext access. No Wi-Fi.
stored_on_device: Optional session key (newer firmware; unverified here)

factory_reset.description:
A hardware gesture that needs three inputs and a power cycle in the middle of it, which is why it reads oddly: throttle and brake held down while the scooter is switched OFF, released, and then the scooter powered back on with a three-second hold.
The app carries a restore-to-factory-settings action too, which is the gentler route when the scooter still talks to a phone. Reach for the hardware one when it does not.
The register-level protocol this spec documents lives on the ESC and BMS behind the Nordic UART bridge; the reset returns those settings to defaults rather than changing the protocol itself.
factory_reset.effect: Restores every setting to factory values, and explicitly includes the Bluetooth connection state and the Bluetooth password. Any client holding pairing state for the scooter has to start again.

procedures.basis: Community reset documentation covering the Ninebot KickScooter ES range. Not performed here; the vendor manual documents the power button but not this combination.
procedures.name: Throttle and brake held across a power cycle

steps.action: Switch the scooter on with the power button.
Hold the throttle and the brake lever fully down and keep them there.
Switch the scooter off while still holding them, then release.
Press the power key for three seconds to switch the scooter back on.
steps.expect: All settings, including the Bluetooth connection and password, are back to factory values.

procedures.basis: The Segway-Ninebot app's own settings menu, as documented by community guides.
procedures.name: Restore to factory settings from the vendor app

steps.action: Connect the scooter to the Segway-Ninebot app over Bluetooth.
In Settings, choose the restore-to-factory-settings entry and confirm.

methods.description: Manual model selection is the first gate. After connecting to that manually selected scooter, use a read-only register request as the post-connect protocol check. Never use NUS or a bare 5A A5 header to choose this spec, and stop if the reply has the Ninebot Z role addresses or repeating-XOR payload transform.

steps.action: Manually select the exact Ninebot/Segway scooter model; do not rely on NUS or the outer frame for identity.
Connect and subscribe to the TX characteristic (6e400003-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e), without writing yet.
After manual model confirmation, send only a read-only 5A A5 register request and validate the scooter role addresses and register reply before any setting write.
steps.expect: A plaintext scooter register reply with the expected ESC/BMS role address and register layout; otherwise stop and do not issue further writes.

setup.notes: NUS is not identity. A person must manually select the exact scooter before any GATT write. Only then connect, subscribe and issue a read-only register request; validate the scooter's role addresses and register reply before any setting write. On newer firmware a session-crypto handshake may be required — verify per unit.

rejoin.notes: No network membership; a new BLE client connects independently.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The Nordic-UART bridge and the 5A A5 frame header are from Informatic/py9b (transport/ninebot.py); the shared register model from CamiAlfa/M365-BLE-PROTOCOL. Newer G30-class firmware is widely reported to add AES session crypto — NOT verified from a source here, so it is flagged, not asserted.

services.name: Nordic UART serial bridge
services.notes: Tunnels the 5A A5 register protocol. Write to 6e400002-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e and read notifications on 6e400003-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e. The register model is shared with xiaomi-m365-ble.yaml. The Ninebot Z uses the same trio, so this is not identity: manual selection and the setup block's read-only protocol check are required before using the write path.
